/-!
# Bridge, part 1: parameters and the field coding

The MIPStarRE development works with a coded field `Fq params := Fin params.q` together
with a `FieldModel params.q` instance carrying an actual field `K` and an equivalence
`K ≃ Fin q`; all arithmetic is transported through the coding (`encodeScalar`,
`decodeScalar`, `addCoord`, ...). This file instantiates that setup for our finite field
`F`: the parameters `lidtParams F m d` (with `q = Fintype.card F`) and the field model
with `K := F`, and it records how the coding interacts with points, lines and the
arithmetic of `F`.
-/

MIPRE.LIDT.Bridge.enc: /-- Encode a scalar of `F` into the coded field of the parameters. -/
MIPRE.LIDT.Bridge.fieldModel: /-- The field model with carrier `F` itself, coded by an arbitrary enumeration. -/
MIPRE.LIDT.Bridge.lidtParams: /-- The MIPStarRE parameters of the `(m, q, d)` test, `q = |F|`. -/
MIPRE.LIDT.Bridge.pointEquiv: /-- The coding of points, as an equivalence. -/
MIPRE.LIDT.Bridge.scalarEquiv: /-- The coding of scalars, as an equivalence. -/

/-!
# Basic finite-dimensional matrix operators

This module contains the elementary trace and matrix-algebra facts used by the
finite-dimensional quantum layer.  It introduces the local operator abbreviation
`Op d = Matrix d d ℂ` and keeps the basic trace bookkeeping independent of the
positive-semidefinite order and normalized-trace material.

## References

The declarations in this file are matrix facts for the LDT
formalization of `references/ldt-paper/`.
-/

MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op: /-- Square complex matrices as the finite-dimensional operator algebra. -/
Matrix.submatrixLinearMap: /-- Taking a submatrix is linear in the ambient matrix.
This packages the entrywise linearity of `Matrix.submatrix` in the same style
as Mathlib's block-diagonal additive and linear maps. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Positive-semidefinite finite matrix order

This module contains the order-theoretic facts for finite-dimensional
complex matrix operators: trace control of positive operators, closedness of the
positive-semidefinite cone, the corresponding `ProperCone`, and basic
monotonicity facts for sandwiches, Kronecker products, and reindexing.

These are the matrix-operator facts used by the canonical SDP strong-duality
argument in Section 9.
-/

MIPStarRE.Quantum.opNonnegativeProperCon: /-- The positive-semidefinite cone in a finite matrix algebra as a proper cone. -/
